title: Finite-diagram and Hom descent from the object and arrow colimits
statement: Let J be a small filtered category and F : J → Cat. Let O be the chosen object-set colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], equipped with a category structure and functors V_j whose object maps are its coprojections and which commute with transitions. Suppose a colimit cocone of the arrow sets is equivalent to Arrow O, intertwining the coprojections with the arrow maps of V_j [def-weil-pbc-arrows-functor]. Then finite lists of objects and arrows lift with every source, target, identity and composition relation; two finite lists with equal images agree at a common refinement; every functor from a finite category lifts to a stage; and the stage Hom sets represent every Hom in O, with equality exactly at a common refinement whose maps out of the starting stage commute.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 09YL (lemma-colimit-sites), first paragraph: 'The formula C = colim C_i means that Ob(C) = colim Ob(C_i) and Arrows(C) = colim Arrows(C_i). Then source, target, and composition are inherited ... Remark that given any finite diagram in C there exists an i such that this diagram is the image of a diagram in C_i' (stated without proof); filtered colimits of sets: categories.tex Section Tag 04AX

proof.text: Choose representatives for the finitely many objects and arrows and representatives for every listed source, target, composition and identity relation. Filteredness gives one stage dominating all of them; applying the transition functors makes every relation hold at that stage. If two lifts are chosen, apply the same eventual-equality clause to their finite list of objects and arrows and then use filteredness to obtain a common later stage where they agree. A functor from a finite category is exactly such a finite list with these relations.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 09YL (09YL), first paragraph and its finite-diagram remark

proof.text: For fixed X,Y in C_j, a morphism in the colimit is represented by an arrow at some j' reached by phi:j -> j'. The source and target equalities can be made literal at a common later stage by the same filtered-colimit equality criterion. Surjectivity follows from arrow representability; injectivity says that two such arrows have equal images exactly when they become equal after a further arrow out of j'. This is precisely the canonical bijection from the filtered colimit over the filtered slice j/J of the Hom sets.
